calendar_note: Planning calendar: weekends and observed U.S. federal holidays, plus recorded custodian closure dates. State/local holidays and special closures can differ. Automatic dates are estimates, not verified legal deadlines.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.label: Initial production / nondisclosure response
AK.summary: State-agency regulation generally requires a response within ten working days for a compliant request. Extensions and fee-related pauses require case-specific review. Local-government rules are not covered by this profile.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.label: Prompt response — no fixed general day count
AZ.summary: Records must be furnished promptly. No general numerical response deadline is inferred; reasonableness depends on the request.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.label: Initial production or written availability response
GA.summary: Available records are generally due within three business days; if responsive records cannot be produced then, a written response must address availability, timing and applicable costs or exemptions. Verify the designated records officer and submission requirements.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.label: Initial acknowledgment / response to an emailed request
IN.summary: Official guidance applies a seven-calendar-day initial-response standard to emailed requests, not a promise of complete production. Verify current agency submission requirements and 2026 APRA amendments, including treatment of out-of-state or automated requests. In-person, telephone and end-date holiday rules require separate review.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.label: Initial written response
MA.summary: Respond within ten business days, counting from the first business day after receipt. A weekend/holiday receipt is treated as received on the following business day. Production schedules and extensions are separate.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.label: Initial written response or extension notice
MI.summary: Email is statutorily received one business day after transmission; the initial response is due five business days after receipt. Junk-folder discovery can change receipt. One written extension of up to ten business days is possible, not automatic. Complete production is a separate issue.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.label: Prompt production — no fixed general day count
NC.summary: Copies must be furnished as promptly as possible. A calendar-based reminder is not proof that a legal deadline was missed. Verify the records custodian.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.label: Initial access, denial, referral or availability notice
NV.summary: By the end of the fifth business day after receipt, provide access or the applicable written custody, availability or denial notice. Verify applicable request forms and custody; a general inquiry may not establish filing.

NY.name: New York
NY.label: Initial access, denial or acknowledgment with estimate
NY.summary: Within five business days, grant, deny, or acknowledge with an approximate response date. Later production dates depend on the acknowledgment and applicable rules; no automatic twenty-day final-production deadline is assumed.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.label: Initial response or written extension notice
PA.summary: Five business days after the agency open-records officer receives a compliant request during regular business hours. After-hours receipt needs review. A written extension may be permitted; never add it without the actual notice. Appeals have separate short deadlines.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.label: Formal written-request response
SD.summary: The formal written-request procedure to the public record officer follows denial of an informal request. It requires a response within ten business days. Do not apply this clock to an unverified general information inquiry.

TX.name: Texas
TX.label: Production / written availability checkpoint
TX.summary: Production must be prompt, which can be earlier than ten business days. If records cannot be produced within ten business days, a written availability certification is required. Attorney-general referral deadlines are different. Agency-designated nonbusiness days and closures require review.

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.label: As soon as practicable — no fixed general day count
WI.summary: Respond as soon as practicable and without delay. Ten working days is guidance for simple, narrow requests, not a universal statutory deadline.

US.name: Federal agencies
US.label: Initial determination — not complete production
US.summary: Generally twenty working days from proper receipt for a determination, excluding weekends and federal holidays. Routing, tolling for clarification/fees and written unusual-circumstances extensions require review. Agency location/time zone may differ.
